summary: In Greek mythology, Clytius (Ancient Greek Κλυτίος) is one of the earthborn Giants who assault Olympus in the Gigantomachy. Apollodorus records that Hecate killed him with torches.
etymology: Greek Κλυτίος; among many mortal and heroic Clytii, this node is the Giant alone.

sections.heading: Slain by Hecate
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 1.6.2) names Clytius among the Giants destroyed when the Olympians fought with Heracles at their side: Hecate kills him with torches. The collective gigantes node holds the earthborn revolt; this node is the individual named in that battle roster.
Vase-painting and later art often show torch-bearing Hecate against a Giant without always labelling him Clytius; the literary pin remains Apollodorus.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id clytius-giant is the Gigantomachy Giant alone. Distinct from Clytius son of Eurytus (Argonaut / Oechalian), Priam's elder brother Clytius, the many suitor Clytii, and other namesakes on the Wikipedia disambiguation list.
